prose: Nikkei Asia reports that China's export controls on critical metals have disrupted supplies of micro drill bits, made mainly from tungsten carbide, which drill tiny holes in printed circuit boards and chip substrates. The controls have sent the price of this little-known tool surging, adding a new link to the AI chip supply-chain squeeze. Only the opening of the article was readable; the rest is behind the page.
highlights: China's critical-metal export controls hit tungsten-carbide micro drill bits
The bits are used in PCBs and chip substrates
Price of the tool has surged, per Nikkei
